prompt: Why didn't Harvard have calculus classes when it first opened?
answer:
Harvard didn’t offer calculus when it opened in 1636 because **calculus had not yet been developed as a formal mathematical discipline**. Isaac Newton and Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz developed their independent versions of calculus several decades later, publishing foundational work in the 1680s.

Harvard’s early curriculum instead emphasized **Latin, Greek, theology, logic, rhetoric, arithmetic, and geometry**—the subjects considered appropriate for training colonial clergy and leaders. Even after calculus emerged, it took time for the new ideas and textbooks to reach the colonies and become part of Harvard’s curriculum.
